content.title: One Day, the World Will Move On Without Us...
content.subtitle: Only our footprints will fade away!
content.body:
Allah says in the Qur'an,

"Every soul shall taste death."

— Surah Aal 'Imran, 3:185

Such a simple and familiar truth, isn't it? Since childhood, we have watched so many people leave this world. Yet as we walk back from a burial, do we ever stop to reflect?

Just moments ago, everyone was calling that person by name. Now they simply say, "the deceased." A few handfuls of soil have turned someone who belonged to this world into a resident of another.

🌿 At the Door of the Grave, Every Identity Ends

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Three things follow the deceased: his family, his wealth, and his deeds. His family and wealth return, while only his deeds remain with him."

— Sahih al-Bukhari, 6514; Sahih Muslim, 2960

The very people for whom we spent our lives striving and sacrificing will one day return home. Shops will open again. Offices will resume. Traffic will fill the streets. Children will go to school. Families will gather around the dinner table.

Slowly, the world moves on. But the grave forgets nothing. No friend will be able to prostrate on our behalf. No loved one will repent for us. No wealth will bring light into the darkness of the grave. Only the deeds we leave behind will remain by our side.

🌿 There Is Still Time

Alhamdulillah, we are not yet residents of that silent grave.

We can still hear the call to Fajr. We can still place our foreheads in sujood. We can still seek forgiveness from others. A hidden charity, a sincere istighfar, or tears shed from a repentant heart may become the very deeds that illuminate our grave.

So do not let today pass like yesterday. Perhaps this sunset will be our last. And if another sunrise awaits us, let it be a morning spent preparing for the Hereafter.

Because one day, the world will truly learn to move on without us. But in the long silence of the grave, our only companion will be our deeds.
